criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Mission purpose, users and rationale are clear and referenced, but no explicit measurable mission requirements are stated, so not complete.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events
report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Gantt/timetable and task descriptions show a feasible plan, but contingency provisions and planned information sources are limited or absent.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
This research will be ongoing throughout almost the entire design process

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Only tutorial/background progress is shown; no preliminary design results or calculations. The orbit statement is technically incorrect.

evidence.quote: geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Readable structure and headings; Gantt is clear but uncaptioned, and references are footnotes/URLs without a full reference list.

evidence.quote: Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue.

technical_issues.issue: States a geostationary orbit at 600 km; GEO altitude is about 35,786 km and 600 km is LEO, so it would not stay fixed over the reef.
No quantified mission requirements such as revisit time, spatial resolution, spectral bands, data latency, coverage or lifetime.
Project plan lacks explicit contingency provisions and planned information sources for launch, orbit and design.
Gantt chart deadlines are unclear; text mentions red deadline lines but chart appears to show only one red line.
STK design starts late in the Gantt chart while the text says simulations will be used throughout.

overall: Mission rationale is strong and referenced, but requirements are not quantified. Plan is feasible yet lacks contingency/sources. Technical progress is minimal and orbit reasoning is wrong. Presentation is readable but references and figure captions are incomplete.

feedback.summary: Your mission rationale is a clear strength: you identify reef-monitoring users and link satellite data to bleaching prediction with references. To reach the next level, quantify requirements, strengthen the plan with contingencies and sources, correct the orbit error, add preliminary technical results, and complete figure captions and a full reference list.
next_steps: In Mission Concept & Rationale, convert goals into measurable requirements (revisit time, spatial resolution, spectral bands, latency, coverage, lifetime) and tie each to user needs; this is what C1 Accomplished requires.

In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, correct the 'geostationary orbit at 600 km' statement (GEO is ~35,786 km; 600 km is LEO), add contingency provisions and planned information sources for launch/orbit/design, and clarify Gantt deadlines/red lines and STK timing.

Add preliminary design results/calculations with brief interpretation, caption Image 1, and replace footnote/URL citations with a full reference list matching in-text citations; these target C3 and C4 Accomplished.

criteria.C1: You clearly explain the reef-monitoring purpose and users, with useful references. However, requirements are not quantified. For Accomplished, state measurable goals/objectives/requirements (revisit, resolution, bands, latency, coverage, lifetime) and explicitly link each mission function to user needs, supported by literature.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt/timetable and task descriptions make the plan believable. To reach Accomplished, add explicit contingency/variation provisions, planned information sources for launch, orbit and design, and explain why the plan fits the mission narrative. Clarify Gantt deadlines and reconcile the late STK start with 'ongoing throughout'.
criteria.C3: You show tutorial progress only, and the 'geostationary orbit at 600 km' statement is technically incorrect. For Accomplished, include a preliminary set of design results/calculations with brief description or interpretation and evidence you are on track; correct the orbit reasoning (GEO ~35,786 km; 600 km is LEO).
criteria.C4: Your headings and structure are readable, and the Gantt is clear. For Accomplished, caption Image 1, ensure all figures/tables are consistently formatted, and provide a full reference list that matches in-text citations; current footnotes/URLs are incomplete. Keep the clear writing style.
